models_evaluated: MedTrustGraph (graph attention encoder + causal GRU + policy engine)

links.outcome: Unauthorized agent actions allowed by calibrated policy layer enforcing patient and purpose scope
links.effect: Policy layer allowed 0 of 652 unauthorized events (95% CI 0–0.59%), auto-allowed 98.64% of authorized events, 1.90% verification workload; synthetic labels make results upper bounds.
links.quote: The calibrated policy layer allowed 0 of 652 unauthorized events (95% CI 0–0.59%) and auto-allowed 98.64% of authorized events with a 1.90% verification workload.

links.outcome: Detection of unauthorized agent actions with versus without patient and purpose context checks
links.effect: Full model F1 0.9653; removing patient context lowered F1 by 0.2173 and purpose context by 0.0200 (Holm-adjusted p<10^-4). Labels derived from scope rules, so upper bounds.
links.quote: In a controlled ablation configuration the full model reached F1 =0.9653 (95% CI 0.9544–0.9741); removing patient context, purpose context, graph structure or temporal structure lowered F1 by 0.2173, 0.0200, 0.0188 and 0.0174 (all Holm-adjusted p<10  <sup>−4</sup>  ).

Separating learned risk scoring from a deterministic policy engine with ALLOW/VERIFY/DENY decisions

screen.reason: Evaluates MedTrustGraph as a continuous zero-trust authorization guardrail / policy engine for clinical LLM agents executing EHR tasks, benchmarked against synthetic agent trajectories to prevent unauthorized actions.

primary.practice: zero-trust continuous authorization guardrail for clinical LLM agents
